question: What tree is venerated during the Sarhul festival, considered the abode of Sarna Maa?
solution:
The Correct Answer is ​__**Sal tree**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Adivasis in Jharkhand and the larger Chhotanagpur region will welcome the new year and the spring season with the Sarhul festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Sarhul** means **worship of the Sal tree** and celebrates the union of the Sun and the Earth.

 
 
• 
 
It marks the beginning of agricultural activities for Adivasis in Jharkhand and the Chhotanagpur region.

 
 
• 
 
**Sal trees (Shorea robusta)** are venerated as the abode of **Sarna Maa**, the deity who protects villages from natural forces.

 
 
• 
 
The festival lasts **3 days**, with main rituals on day two at **Sarna Sthals** (sacred groves near villages).

 
 
• 
 
**Tribes like Oraon, Munda, Santal, Khadia, and Ho** celebrate Sarhul with unique traditions.

 
 
• 
 
Sarhul evolved from a **hunting tradition** to a focus on **agriculture**.

 
 
• 
 
The festival has spread to regions like **Assam, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Nepal, Bangladesh, and Bhutan**.
